_readme: The subject of the benchmark. `scripts/evaluate.py --model` defaults to `current.hf_model`,
so 'evaluate the model' has one unambiguous answer and a comparison always names what it
is comparing against what.
This file is DATA, not a claim of quality in the abstract. `reason` states what the
designation rests on, `evidence` says where to check it, and `qualification` states what
the designation does NOT mean. Change it in a deliberate commit that cites new evidence --
never as a side effect of a run, and never by a script. Nothing in this repo writes it.
CONFIRMED REGRESSION, 2026-08-29 (same day as publish): this checkpoint (and the copy
currently live on the Hub at episod/tt-tnt-1024) was retrained with `--tokens-dir
artifacts/tokens-v3` -- the corpus generation from BEFORE the dialogue slice
(databricks-dolly-15k) was added. artifacts/tokens-v4 is the correct, current corpus
(docs/corpus_blend.md confirms this explicitly). Verified directly: greedy-decoded
'Q: What is the capital of France?\nAnswer:' now produces repetitive non-answers
('Cantons, Cantons, Cantons...') instead of the dialogue checkpoint's correct 'Paris'.
A corrected retrain on tokens-v4 (artifacts/checkpoints-tt-tnt-1024-ctx2048-v4corpus) is
in progress -- re-publish once it passes the same Q&A check. Until then, treat this
designation's Q&A/dialogue capability claim as KNOWN FALSE, not merely unverified.
AS OF 2026-08-29 (path convention): `hf_model` is `artifacts/hf-tt-tnt-1024` -- ONE fixed directory that
gets overwritten with whatever the current best idea for this size is, rather than a new
`-dialogue`/`-editor`/`-ctx2048`-suffixed sibling per experiment. That sprawl (a dozen-plus
`artifacts/hf-tt-tnt-1024-*` directories, several documented negative results left sitting
alongside the real one) was consolidated away in a deliberate cleanup -- see CLAUDE.md's
2026-08-29 entry for what was removed and why. A checkpoint worth keeping as a distinct,
citable artifact going forward gets that argued for explicitly, not created by default.
The raw training checkpoints under artifacts/checkpoints-* are untouched by this -- only
the derived, cheaply-regeneratable HF conversions were collapsed to one.

current.label: tt-tnt-1024
current.reason: Retrained the prior dialogue-trained checkpoint's lineage at a 2048-token context (up from 512), specifically to hold conversations far out of reach of a real, reproduced growing-conversation KV-cache crash confirmed to be a generic tt-metal/vLLM defect -- not this project's model -- by reproducing the identical failure on stock meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct at the same context size (docs/upstream-tt-metal-asks.md entry 6). Also ships a chat template baked into tokenizer_config.json that caps rendered conversation history to the last 5 messages, the proven-safe boundary from direct reproduction, as a backstop regardless of context size. At a matched 512-token window, loss improved -0.2318 nats against the prior checkpoint (2.7726 -> 2.5408).
current.qualification: CONFIRMED REGRESSION as of 2026-08-29 (see the _readme note above): this checkpoint was trained on the wrong corpus generation (tokens-v3, predating the dialogue slice) and has measurably LOST the Q&A capability the checkpoint it replaces was designated for -- greedy-decoded 'capital of France' now loops on 'Cantons, Cantons, Cantons...' instead of answering 'Paris'. A corrected retrain on tokens-v4 is in progress; do not treat this designation's dialogue capability as intact until that lands and is verified. Not unqualified, and not a claim of behavioural improvement: no signal in the paired comparison against the prior checkpoint clears both the seed-only noise floor and its own paired minimum-detectable difference, in either direction, at n=1 seed -- this is a real loss gain and a clean behavioural null, not a behavioural win. The prior checkpoint's own known regression (4-gram repeat rate worse than tt-tnt-1024a at 3.32x the seed floor) is therefore neither confirmed fixed nor newly measured here. This checkpoint was trained at a 2048-token window; the prior one it replaces was trained and measured at 512 -- this project has already published one wrong headline from treating a 512-window loss and a 2048-window loss as commensurable, so the matched-window comparison above is deliberately re-measured at 512 rather than diffing the two training-time trajectories directly. The MoE routing, die-region routing, thinking, skits, and reach-dial experiments described in docs/model-card-1024.md were run against the PRIOR 512-context checkpoint this one was retrained from, and have not been re-verified against these specific weights.
